title: Model names got a more reliable map
summary:
A week of making model names more dependable, refreshing the models behind them, and giving people more ways to build with the results.

Aliases now resolve to their intended service models, including for Enter’s free-usage checks and generation prices. Registry checks also catch invalid service IDs and missing model IDs instead of silently falling through. `openai-large` now maps to `gpt-5-chat-latest`, while the image registry recognizes `gptimage`, `gpt-image`, and `gpt-image-1-mini`.

`gptimage` returned for seed-tier generation and editing, then split its work between `gpt-image-1-mini` for generation and `gpt-image-1` for edits. `kontext` moved to Azure Flux Kontext for generation and editing, with a 1024-pixel maximum side length. Nano Banana was added as a nectar-tier image model, and the image API gained an `/about` endpoint for model details.

`deepseek` moved to DeepSeek V3.1 with hybrid reasoning, and former reasoning names remain as aliases. `mistral` moved to Small 3.2; `mistral-naughty` replaced the `mistral-romance` listing while preserving the old name as an alias. `openai-audio` now accepts up to 10,000 input characters and 6,384 completion tokens. The docs also clarify GPT-5 parameter limits and offer prompting guidance for reasoning models and verbatim TTS.

A growing Pollen FAQ now covers grants, wallets, Quests, model access, and image output per Pollen. Balance and API-key screens received clearer labels and layouts, key descriptions now appear where expected, and sign-in and account pages adapt to phones. Enter also uses the tier stored in a user’s session for generation tracking; that change does not add tier-based usage enforcement.
